approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves scored molecular graphs. It samples breeding parents from high-score population groups, applies its existing crossover and mutations, and builds a surplus pool of fresh valid identities. A Gaussian process trained on all accepted raw scores uses count fingerprints and a Tanimoto kernel. For each evaluation slot it draws a correlated score function across that pool and picks the best still-available molecule. Real accepted outcomes alone update the model archive and score-ranked survivors. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is already disabled; ordinary mutations and their continuation remain active.
approach.novelty: Add incumbent-referenced expected batch improvement: reuse one fixed panel of joint posterior scenarios, begin every scenario at the best raw score already accepted, and choose each molecule for its remaining positive contribution to that batch improvement. This targets progress beyond the current best while accounting for score peaks covered by earlier batch choices. Earlier shared-panel and antithetic experiments maximized an unthresholded batch maximum under an older Parent. Current siblings have tested representation, predictive targets, generation, feedback and selector removals; none supplies a formally evaluated current-Parent unthresholded shared-panel control. This experiment therefore tests the complete new allocation rule against the Parent. The same-panel unthresholded comparison explains decision differences without claiming an isolated endpoint effect of the threshold.

hypothesis: Replace successful independent-row posterior allocation with greedy incumbent-referenced expected batch improvement over one fixed 128-or-announced-batch-size shared joint posterior panel, using only the best previously accepted raw score and exact smallest-index ties.

finding_summary.headline: Incumbent targeting raises sampled batch utility, but smaller real gains lower all three seed means
finding_summary.insights:
The experiment exposes a failure of the complete incumbent-referenced allocation rule under this Parent: correct positive-improvement targeting and higher sampled utility did not deliver larger real advances. More update events again accompanied smaller increments. The mean realized batch-improvement contrast telescopes to the final-score contrast on these equal-length streams, so those two failures should not be counted as independent endpoint evidence. The result supports a negative contribution from this whole rule under the tested composition. A threshold-only endpoint effect remains unresolved because the current unthresholded comparison has no separately evaluated future trajectory.

Finite-panel zero gain also failed to identify unproductive molecules. Fourteen zero-gain choices beat their frozen real incumbent, eleven made sequential incumbent updates, 205 were later bred and 119 survived to the final populations. Two became session leaders. Every one of those fourteen real wins had no sampled scenario above the incumbent. The chemical report includes a ring-free urea/enamide/thiocarbonyl leader and a distinct aza-dicarbonyl leader in this group. These are concrete limits of the sampled improvement support; they do not establish whether model error, finite tail sampling, myopic selection or later breeding caused the overall loss.

Selected-stream MSE and interval coverage improved while within-batch ordering weakened, but the selected molecules and histories changed. Those diagnostics do not establish repaired uncertainty or improved chemistry. Familiar amines and lactams still coexist with reactive bonds, difficult rings, large assemblies and unspecified stereochemistry. The older unthresholded and antithetic failures retain their exchange-containing Parent conditions, and shared-Parent siblings supply no isolated threshold, additive or joint-component effect. The complete exposed endpoint failure supplies the registered approach-review evidence without authorizing acquisition tuning.
finding_summary.results:
The allocation mechanism executed and changed real decisions. All 435 frozen incumbents, 128-row posterior panels and 4,350 exact greedy choices passed independent reconstruction. There were 3,681 positive-gain choices and 669 exact-zero choices; 23 complete batches had zero sampled improvement from their first position. Every zero choice followed the registered smallest-index tie rule without a fallback. All 435 selected sets differed from the Parent rule on the same panels. Mean sampled batch-improvement utility rose by 0.005726: 371 batches improved, 64 tied and none declined. Against the unthresholded shared-panel rule, 343 sets changed and mean utility rose by 0.000256, with fifteen contrary losses.

Real progress moved the other way. Average realized batch improvement fell from 0.013351 to 0.011410. Advancing batches rose from 202 to 204 and sequential incumbent updates from 258 to 270, but mean positive batch gain fell from 0.028751 to 0.024331. Mean accepted offspring score also fell, from 0.385256 to 0.351177. All evaluations completed, yet final mean score fell from 0.595670 to 0.539394, a paired change of -0.056276 against the required +0.002. Seed changes were -0.092867, -0.016706 and -0.059254. Nine task-seed endpoints declined and six improved, including all three median-similarity endpoints.

molecular.headline: Aryl amines and bridged lactams persist; an acyclic sulfur/urea chain leads one task despite zero sampled marginal gain
molecular.overall_character: All five objectives and all three issued Search seeds were inspected for Child n-8a62df15e51f and code Parent n-62daf219c70a. Each node has 4,500 evaluated records, including 4,350 optimizer products; every task contributes 900 records and 870 optimizer products. context.comparison establishes both complete Child evaluation and complete matched Parent pairing, with no profile mismatch or missing trajectory. All fifteen paired trajectories differ; common molecular identities retain consistent recorded scores. The actual resource receipt records three completed replicas with six CPUs, 16,000 MB and one A40 each. The supplied full-panel mean is 0.5393940797230263 versus 0.5956696497334577, with paired seed changes -0.09286669965406602,-0.016705653920698005 and -0.05925435645652999. All three median-similarity endpoints improve, while several other endpoints fall; these contrary cases remain in the per-task comparisons. These are recorded evaluation outcomes, not an activation, eligibility or component-contribution decision. The molecules remain rich in aromatic and heterocyclic frameworks: indole carboxamides, linked halogenated heteroaryls, cyclic and macrocyclic amines, ether/lactam bridges and aza-dicarbonyl cores. A conspicuous exception is an acyclic urea/enamide/ketone/thioaldehyde leader. Median heavy-atom counts in fixed task order are 25,37,29,31,26, versus Parent 25,33,31,30,27. The overall median is four perceived rings and two aromatic rings. Digest ring-string presence ranges from 0.8931 to 0.9862 and aromatic-string presence from 0.8034 to 0.9782; these are molecule-level text counters, not geometry or aromatic atom fractions. The lowest aromatic fraction belongs to the population containing the acyclic leader, so its ring-free chemistry must not be hidden by the overall ring-rich description. Within-seed upper-score neighborhoods are usually much narrower than the complete panel. Familiar functional groups coexist with chemical liabilities. Counts of optimizer molecules with N-halogen/O-halogen/O-O bonds are 437/109/75 for the Child versus 1,042/278/273 for the Parent. This decrease in specific motifs does not establish a global feasibility improvement: the Child has 147 molecules containing a ring carbon with at least two double bonds, versus 42 in the Parent, and also produces aryl cyanates, terminal C=S groups, N-S substitution, crowded aminals, short unsaturated rings and dense bridges. Not every carbon with two double bonds is the same kind of cumulene; the concrete cyclic carbon-chain examples are identified below. No Child evaluated molecule has a ring triple bond, but that is not evidence of its absence from unscored pools or the unchanged generator's support. There are 124 products with at most three heavy atoms versus Parent 99, alongside evaluated structures as large as 120 heavy atoms. All digest stereocentre-marker rates are zero, while RDKit identifies unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,391 Child and 2,408 Parent optimizer rows. Ring perception, sanitization and a score do not establish a synthesis, stability, accessible conformation, safety or a preferred stereoisomer. Actual molecule provenance was joined through pool identity, emitted prediction, accepted score, survivor population and later parent reuse in all thirty logs. The Child and Parent each construct 69,600 pool records and evaluate 4,350 optimizer products. Every one of the 435 Child suggestions freezes its incumbent from the complete preceding accepted raw-score archive; all exact tied records and the smallest-serial representative match that history. The representative is an initial molecule in 17 batches and an earlier accepted offspring in 418; 53 batches have multiple incumbent ties. It is neither the generating-parent score nor a posterior prediction or future observation. The fixed recorded panel has 128 joint function-value rows in each batch. All active marginal vectors, masks, chosen identities and exact tie choices were checked against that panel without generating new draws or scores. The prediction mean and standard deviation remain raw-score moments; posterior_sample is a passive panel-row value, separate from the optimizing marginal increment. There are 3,681 positive-marginal and 669 exact-zero-marginal evaluated choices. The latter occur in 96 batches, including 23 wholly zero batches, and select the smallest remaining original pool index. This is normal finite-panel saturation, not numerical fallback; no fallback occurred. The zero cohort contains 70 acyclic products and 24 tiny fragments, but also substantial useful-scoring molecules: 59 beat their best generating parent, 14 exceed the batch's frozen incumbent, 11 update the running incumbent, 355 survive their batch, 119 remain in the final population and 205 are later bred. Only four of these zero-marginal choices have any panel row above the original incumbent; later marginal saturation can also occur after earlier choices already cover those rows. Zero finite-panel utility therefore does not show chemical absence or lack of real improvement potential. Two session leaders come from zero-marginal ties. The acyclic leader in seed 1 of the final task is evaluation 194, position 3/pool index 3 in wholly saturated batch 19. Its frozen incumbent is the earlier accepted evaluation 143 at 0.3487520004285424, drawn from 190 preceding accepted records; its generating parent is a different molecule at 0.2624259366847637. The leader scores 0.43419030554852406 after an append and ring opening. Seed 2/evaluation 158 is likewise a zero choice, scoring 0.4189666353060081 after a fluorine append to a small-ring dicarbonyl family. Both are molecular counterexamples to treating zero sampled marginal gain as useless chemistry, but neither identifies a beneficial causal contribution from the tie rule or the acquisition threshold. All 435 same-panel passive controls are available. The unthresholded rule changes its batch set relative to the actual choices in 343 batches; the independent-row rule changes all 435. Their complete sequences were checked on their own masks, separately from same-active-prefix diagnostics. Unevaluated alternatives receive no labels, chemical-outcome claims or hypothetical future histories. The actual scored Child has 632 best-parent beats and 270 incumbent updates versus Parent 629 and 258, while mean realized improvement over the frozen batch incumbent is 0.011410412713128188 versus 0.013350949610039598. Counts of local wins, internal panel utilities and selected chemistry are different observations; none alone explains the lower complete endpoints. Historical unthresholded n-9c0f6fa601f8 and antithetic n-0db88abff519 retain their original exchange-containing Parent n-559d25e9c9c7 and paired means -0.0003646022443066406 and -0.016104112533858978. Both had opposing seed effects; the antithetic variant also used a different zero-gain mean-completion rule. They are conditional counterexamples, not independent tests on the present exchange-free Parent. Current rank-target n-ae12ccae8c7b and magnitude-credit n-9d0376974738 likewise retain their negative endpoint results despite favorable local progress measurements. per_task.generated_character: Better products are compact indole carboxamides with a separate phenyl or pyridyl surface and methoxy, methyl or vinyl substituents. The top fifty have 23-26 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings. Seed 0's leader has an N-amino indole, bromomethyl group and fluorophenyl amide. Seed 1 has a vinyl/methoxy indole with an N-S-substituted pyridyl amide. Seed 2's 24-heavy-atom leader carries an enol-like vinyl alcohol and an amide nitrogen/methylene bridge spanning a pyridyl ring; its five perceived rings do not make this bridge a routine saturated amine. N-halogen bonds are much less prevalent than in the Parent: 128 versus 445 optimizer products, although still present in 19 of the highest fifty. Parent leaders used related aromatic carbonyl frameworks, including N-fluoro, N-hydroxyamide and diketone chemistry. The shift changes local liabilities without eliminating them.
liabilities: Bromomethyl substitution, N-amino indole, N-S-substituted amide and residual N-Cl/N-Br amides warrant distinct chemical scrutiny; they are not interchangeable with ordinary aryl halogenation.
The short amide-N/methylene bridge across a pyridyl ring constrains geometry. The leader’s enol-like group adds a tautomeric question that is not resolved by its recorded score.
missing_features: The small poor products lack the combined aromatic surfaces and compact carbonyl connection found in better molecules. The leading excerpt offers limited routine alternatives preserving that spacing without short pyridyl-spanning bridges, N-S/N-N substitution or halomethyl groups.
The enol-bearing and bridged products do not establish stable tautomeric or accessible three-dimensional alternatives. The scalar records identify no mandatory missing target-specific group.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In the current complete panel, 669 actual evaluated choices have zero marginal gain; 14 exceed their frozen accepted incumbent and 205 are later bred. Two session leaders are zero choices, including an acyclic urea/enamide/thiocarbonyl product made by appending and opening a ring. Its accepted precursor and the distinct earlier incumbent are exactly joined. This narrows the output limitation to a mismatch between some observed molecular transformations and their sampled improvement support. The historic n-9c0f6fa601f8 and n-0db88abff519 results remain conditional on their exchange-containing Parent and different allocation laws; no current-Parent unthresholded scored sibling isolates the threshold here.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically informative accepted molecules can lie outside all positive finite-panel improvement scenarios, so zero sampled value does not identify unproductive chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Retain chemical provenance and real feedback for novel transformations even when the finite panel assigns zero marginal value. Distinguish ring opening that retains a distributed polar framework from destructive fragmentation; neither a new chemistry ban nor a claim about unscored alternatives follows from the zero class. Any future allocation interpretation must preserve the complete-law and historical comparison limits.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The n-c55c3d520a2c chemistry gap, reproduced by Parent n-62daf219c70a, remains with a changed balance: N-X/O-X/O-O occurrences decrease to 437/109/75, while ring carbons with at least two double bonds occur in 147 evaluated products versus Parent 42. transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand chemically conventional alternatives preserving accepted molecules’ ring, amine and carbonyl relationships, with task-agnostic feedback assessing their value. In contrast, one ring-free 24-heavy-atom product leads its session and several compact amine or carbonyl frameworks score well. The evidence therefore concerns maintenance of a useful distributed architecture, not a universal ring-retention or size-minimization rule. This refines the existing n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a whole-molecule plausibility gap without assigning an endpoint effect to any edit.
transferable_gaps.gap: Scaffold size and functional-group relationships are not consistently preserved across fragmentation, ring edits and molecular enlargement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support controlled changes of connectivity while retaining and contrasting complete accepted functional-group arrangements. Separate useful ring opening from collapse and avoid equating repeated motifs with useful added chemistry. Validate the actual resulting molecules through authorized feedback; unselected pool outcomes remain unknown.

transferable_gaps.evidence: As in n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a, every current digest stereocentre-marker rate is zero. RDKit nevertheless finds unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,391 of 4,350 optimizer products, including every molecule in two highest-fifty excerpts and both saturated/cyclobutene and bridged lactam leaders. The acyclic thiocarbonyl leader also lacks specified alkene geometry. These are observations about evaluated representations, not proof that all potential configurations are stable or absent from every unscored generated structure.
transferable_gaps.gap: Evaluated stereochemical and geometric alternatives remain unspecified despite abundant saturated, bridged and heteroatom-adjacent centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and preserve meaningful stereochemical and alkene-geometric distinctions where the actual graph supports them, then use allowed feedback to assess their value. method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

finding_summary.headline: Incumbent targeting raises sampled batch utility, but smaller real gains lower all three seed means
finding_summary.insights:
The experiment exposes a failure of the complete incumbent-referenced allocation rule under this Parent: correct positive-improvement targeting and higher sampled utility did not deliver larger real advances. More update events again accompanied smaller increments. The mean realized batch-improvement contrast telescopes to the final-score contrast on these equal-length streams, so those two failures should not be counted as independent endpoint evidence. The result supports a negative contribution from this whole rule under the tested composition. A threshold-only endpoint effect remains unresolved because the current unthresholded comparison has no separately evaluated future trajectory.

Finite-panel zero gain also failed to identify unproductive molecules. Fourteen zero-gain choices beat their frozen real incumbent, eleven made sequential incumbent updates, 205 were later bred and 119 survived to the final populations. Two became session leaders. Every one of those fourteen real wins had no sampled scenario above the incumbent. The chemical report includes a ring-free urea/enamide/thiocarbonyl leader and a distinct aza-dicarbonyl leader in this group. These are concrete limits of the sampled improvement support; they do not establish whether model error, finite tail sampling, myopic selection or later breeding caused the overall loss.

Selected-stream MSE and interval coverage improved while within-batch ordering weakened, but the selected molecules and histories changed. Those diagnostics do not establish repaired uncertainty or improved chemistry. Familiar amines and lactams still coexist with reactive bonds, difficult rings, large assemblies and unspecified stereochemistry. The older unthresholded and antithetic failures retain their exchange-containing Parent conditions, and shared-Parent siblings supply no isolated threshold, additive or joint-component effect. The complete exposed endpoint failure supplies the registered approach-review evidence without authorizing acquisition tuning.
finding_summary.results:
The allocation mechanism executed and changed real decisions. All 435 frozen incumbents, 128-row posterior panels and 4,350 exact greedy choices passed independent reconstruction. There were 3,681 positive-gain choices and 669 exact-zero choices; 23 complete batches had zero sampled improvement from their first position. Every zero choice followed the registered smallest-index tie rule without a fallback. All 435 selected sets differed from the Parent rule on the same panels. Mean sampled batch-improvement utility rose by 0.005726: 371 batches improved, 64 tied and none declined. Against the unthresholded shared-panel rule, 343 sets changed and mean utility rose by 0.000256, with fifteen contrary losses.

Real progress moved the other way. Average realized batch improvement fell from 0.013351 to 0.011410. Advancing batches rose from 202 to 204 and sequential incumbent updates from 258 to 270, but mean positive batch gain fell from 0.028751 to 0.024331. Mean accepted offspring score also fell, from 0.385256 to 0.351177. All evaluations completed, yet final mean score fell from 0.595670 to 0.539394, a paired change of -0.056276 against the required +0.002. Seed changes were -0.092867, -0.016706 and -0.059254. Nine task-seed endpoints declined and six improved, including all three median-similarity endpoints.

It also shows why more parent-beating offspring and more incumbent updates are insufficient evidence of stronger final solutions: they can be more frequent increments along a weaker search history.
